scope: Seven IntelliJ-native read operations (find_file, search_symbols, get_file_outline, get_symbol_info, find_references, read_file, search_text) as a platform-free Java typed argument and outcome domain, a session-local handle and page-token registry, and IntelliJ read adapters with indexing readiness, cancellation and bounds. Depends on CAP-LIFECYCLE-ADMISSION and CAP-DOMAIN-RUN-DRIVER. Wire JSON argument parsing, tool schemas, the LLM status/code/content envelope and rendering of read outcomes into ToolOutcome content are excluded and belong to the Codex codec feature.

requirements.statement: The read catalog is exactly seven operations: find_file, search_symbols, get_file_outline, get_symbol_info, find_references, read_file, search_text. Each operation has its own typed argument value that validates every bound at construction, and no model-visible generic dispatcher exists. The text query arguments are the find_file query, the search_symbols name and the search_text query. Each contains no CR or LF and holds at most 1,000 UTF-16 code units; the find_file and search_text queries are nonempty, and the search_symbols name is empty (SR-006) or a Java identifier. A find_file query contains no '\', does not start or end with '/', and has no empty, '.' or '..' segment. An argument that fails validation is rejected before admission and before any IntelliJ access.

Result bounds: find_file, search_symbols, find_references and search_text accept limit 1–100, default 50; get_file_outline returns pages of at most 100 entries; read_file returns at most 300 lines and 24 KiB of UTF-8; get_symbol_info returns at most 300 lines and 24 KiB of declaration source (SR-008); every match or reference excerpt is at most 500 UTF-16 code units with an explicit truncated flag (SR-010). Paged operations collect at most the result collection cap before sorting; the cap is an injected bound with production value 10,000. When a query has more results than the cap, the operation returns TOO_MANY_RESULTS with a hint to narrow the scope and no page. No result value can exceed its bound.

read_file takes a path, an optional 1-based start line (default 1) and an optional 1-based inclusive end line (default start plus 99). An end before start, or a span above 300 lines, is an argument rejection. Lines are the lines of the current document text with LF terminators; a final LF does not start another line, and an empty document has zero lines. The range is clipped at end of file and the actual range is returned. A start line after the last line, including any start in an empty document, returns RANGE_OUT_OF_BOUNDS with the line count. The 24 KiB cap counts the UTF-8 bytes of the returned lines including their LF terminators. When the cap cuts the range, the result holds the largest whole-line prefix, its actual range and a truncated flag. When the start line alone exceeds 24 KiB, the result is LINE_EXCEEDS_BYTE_CAP with that line's byte size. A binary file, or a file the platform does not load as text content, returns UNSUPPORTED_FILE. A successful read returns a read handle.

A path argument is relative to the project base directory or absolute. The adapter normalizes it (removes '.' and '..' segments, resolves symbolic links) before any check. Project content roots, library source roots, excluded roots and the project base directory are compared in the same canonical form, with symbolic links resolved. The first matching check wins, in this order: (1) the normalized path is not under a project content root or an attached library source root, decided by its nearest existing ancestor, returns OUTSIDE_PROJECT; a file in a library class root (compiled classes) is OUTSIDE_PROJECT; (2) the path is under an excluded root returns EXCLUDED_PATH; (3) no file or directory exists returns FILE_NOT_FOUND; (4) a directory where a file is required returns NOT_A_FILE. A returned path is rendered with '/' separators relative to the canonical project base directory when the file is under it, and otherwise as the platform file URL (for example a jar:// URL for a library source entry); both forms are accepted as path input. Library files are read-only evidence.

find_file takes a query and a scope. The query is an exact case-sensitive file name, or a relative path of one or more whole trailing path segments ending in a file name, matched case-sensitively ('a/B.java' matches '…/a/B.java' and not '…/xa/B.java'). Scope PROJECT (default) covers non-excluded project content except generated sources. Scope LIBRARIES covers PROJECT content plus attached library sources. A generated source is a file for which any GeneratedSourcesFilter reports generated. Each result carries its rendered path (SR-004) and origin PROJECT or LIBRARY. Results are ordered by rendered path.

search_symbols takes a case-sensitive name, a scope PROJECT (default) or LIBRARIES with the SR-005 meaning, and an optional restriction to one file path or one owner type handle. A nonempty name matches a declaration whose simple name is equal to it. Without a restriction, generated sources are omitted in both scopes, and the library candidates of LIBRARIES are declarations in attached library source files; a compiled library class without attached sources is not a candidate. An empty name is valid only with a restriction. A restriction overrides scope and generated-source filtering. A file restriction lists every catalog declaration in that file at any nesting depth; an owner type restriction lists the declarations directly declared in that type, including nested types but not their members and not inherited members. An owner type handle whose element is not a class, interface, enum, record or annotation type returns NOT_A_TYPE. A nonempty name with a restriction matches only inside the restriction. The catalog declaration kinds are Java class, interface, enum, record, annotation type, method, constructor, field and enum constant written in source. Local classes, anonymous classes, any declaration inside a local class, anonymous class or enum-constant body, record components, implicit constructors, initializers and lambdas are not declarations. A constructor matches the name of its class. Each matching declaration is a separate candidate with symbol handle, language, kind, name, qualified owner, signature, rendered path and declaration range (SR-025). Overloads and unrelated same-name types are never merged or reduced to a first match.

get_file_outline takes one file path and returns the catalog declarations (SR-006) of that file in source order, at any nesting depth, each with nesting depth (the number of enclosing catalog declarations, so 0 for top-level types), kind, name, signature, declaration range (SR-025) and symbol handle, in pages of at most 100 entries. It returns no statements or expression nodes. It never resolves types, so it needs no index. A non-Java file returns UNSUPPORTED_LANGUAGE, never an empty success.

get_symbol_info takes a symbol handle and returns the symbol identity (kind, name, qualified owner, signature), declaration range (SR-025), the current document version, and either the declaration source with a new read handle for exactly that range, or SOURCE_TOO_LARGE with the declaration line count and UTF-8 byte size and no source and no read handle when the declaration exceeds 300 lines or 24 KiB.

find_references takes a symbol handle and a scope PROJECT (default) or LIBRARIES with the SR-005 meaning, except that references inside generated sources are included and marked generated. It returns every platform PsiReference in scope that resolves to the element, including import statements, Javadoc references ({@link}, @see) and references from non-Java files. A reference that resolves to a compiled library declaration is a reference to the equivalent declaration in its attached library source. Method search is strict: calls through a super method, calls to overriding methods and calls to overloads are not references to the handle's method. Every page carries the re-resolved target identity (kind, name, qualified owner, signature, declaration range and current document version, as in SR-008) and the scope used. Each reference has rendered path, a range of 0-based start and end-exclusive UTF-16 document offsets (the reference element start offset plus the reference range in that element), the 1-based line of the range start, a line excerpt (SR-010 excerpt rule with the range start as match start), a generated flag, a kind and the containing declaration (SR-025), absent when no catalog declaration encloses the reference. The kind is IMPORT for a reference inside a Java import statement, DOC for a reference inside a Java doc comment, and CODE otherwise. Unresolved text in comments or string literals and identifiers that resolve to a different element are not references. Results are ordered by rendered path, then start offset.

search_text takes a required scope path (SR-004) and a literal query (SR-001), matched case-sensitively; regex is excluded. A directory scope searches its files recursively and omits excluded, generated and binary files; text files too large for content loading are omitted and counted in a skipped-file count carried on every page. A file scope searches that file; a binary file scope, or a file scope that the platform does not load as text content, returns UNSUPPORTED_FILE. The search reads current document text, including unsaved changes. Each non-overlapping match, scanned left to right, is one result with rendered path, 1-based line, start and end offsets as 0-based end-exclusive UTF-16 document offsets, and an excerpt. The match column is the match start offset minus the start offset of its line. The excerpt is the whole line when it has at most 500 UTF-16 code units; otherwise it is the 500-unit window starting at column max(0, min(matchColumn − 100, lineLength − 500)) with truncated set, shortened by one unit at each end that splits a surrogate pair. Results are ordered by rendered path, then start offset.

Symbol handles are issued only by the adapter from IntelliJ resolution results of catalog operations. A handle is an opaque session-scoped identifier that encodes no PSI pointer, path, offset or source text. The adapter payload of a symbol handle holds the smart pointer plus language, qualified owner, signature, file identity and the document modification stamp observed at issue. Before issuing, the adapter compares the new pointer with live symbol entries using SmartPointerManager.pointToTheSameElement and returns the existing handle when one matches.

One session-local registry holds symbol handles, read handles and page tokens with a total bound of 2,048 entries and least-recently-used eviction; issuing, reusing (SR-011) or successfully looking up an entry refreshes its recency. Each entry has one kind (symbol handle, read handle or page token), and each lookup is for one kind; an identifier of another kind is unknown to that lookup. The registry domain type is generic over an opaque payload type supplied by the adapter; it never inspects or compares payloads and invokes the adapter release action on eviction and disposal. An evicted, unknown, wrong-kind or other-session symbol or read handle returns STALE_HANDLE with a rediscovery hint; an evicted, unknown, wrong-kind or other-session page token returns STALE_PAGE. An issue on a disposed registry registers nothing and returns a disposed result.

A read operation on a symbol handle re-resolves the stored smart pointer inside its read computation with documents committed. If the element no longer exists, or the restored element's kind, name or signature differs from the handle payload, it returns STALE_HANDLE. If the element still exists after document edits with the same kind, name and signature, the operation uses the element's current state and reports the current document version.

A read handle is an immutable value of file identity, the document modification stamp observed at the read, and the exact inspected line and offset ranges; construction rejects a start after its end, negative offsets and line values below 1. get_symbol_info and read_file create read handles. This feature performs no mutation with a read handle.

Current editor content is authoritative. Every operation computes its result inside one read computation that runs only when all documents are committed (the platform documents-committed constraint), so every returned text and range comes from the current document including unsaved changes, and every PSI range matches the reported document version. The document version is the document modification stamp.

Index-backed operations (find_file, search_symbols, get_symbol_info, find_references, search_text) run their read computation under the platform smart-mode constraint, and every index-backed platform call, including reference search, runs inside that read computation and never outside read access. The total wait for smart mode, including restarts after dumb mode begins during the computation, is bounded by the index wait bound: an injected duration with production value 30 seconds. DumbService.waitForSmartMode(long) is not used. At the bound the operation returns INDEX_NOT_READY with a retry hint and no partial result. An IndexNotReadyException that escapes the computation also returns INDEX_NOT_READY with no partial result. A write action that cancels a read computation restarts it; time spent in these restarts does not count toward the index wait bound and has no bound, and only cancellation (SR-019) ends it. read_file and get_file_outline do not wait for indexing. A closed, disposed or not-yet-initialized project returns PROJECT_UNAVAILABLE. No operation returns an empty success because indexes were unavailable.

The paged operations are find_file, search_symbols, get_file_outline, find_references and search_text. A page result is either complete or has more results with a next-page token. A page token is a registry entry (SR-012) bound to the operation, the full argument set without the token, the session registry, the PSI modification count observed when the first page was computed, and the next offset. A next-page request repeats the argument set and adds the token; a different limit is a different argument set. Each page result that has more results issues a new token for the following page. A token stays valid after use: while it is live and still matches, a repeated request with it returns the same page again. A next-page request returns STALE_PAGE when the token is unknown, evicted, of another kind or from another registry, when the operation or argument set differs, or when the PSI modification count differs. The count is compared before any wait for indexing (SR-026), in a read computation with documents committed, and again inside the operation's read computation. Because computations run with committed documents (SR-015), unsaved edits change the count. Dumb-mode entry and exit also change the count, so indexing between pages returns STALE_PAGE by design, without a wait. Ordering is deterministic within one modification count.

Semantic operations support Java only. Symbol handles exist only for Java declarations of the SR-006 kinds, and search_symbols returns only Java declarations. get_file_outline on a non-Java file and search_symbols restricted to a non-Java file return UNSUPPORTED_LANGUAGE. find_references on a Java symbol includes resolved references from non-Java files (SR-009). read_file, find_file and search_text work for any text file.

Each read is one admitted executable call. The read executor receives the CallAdmission and RunCancellation that the ToolRunner passes and calls CallAdmission.execute exactly once off the EDT. When execute returns Limited or Rejected, the Effect did not run, no IntelliJ access happens, and the read executor returns a typed NotAdmitted result that carries the admission result; the codec feature maps it to ToolOutcome.NotStarted with RUN_LIMIT_NOT_STARTED for Limited and CANCELLED_NOT_STARTED for Rejected. The Effect contains the index wait and the whole read computation, and it returns or throws only after the platform read computation for this call has terminated. The run cancellation token cancels the wait and the computation; the listener registered on RunCancellation only requests that cancellation and never blocks, because RunSession runs listeners under its monitor, possibly on the EDT. On cancellation, including content close, the Effect throws java.util.concurrent.CancellationException, so the lifecycle records FAILED_AFTER_START and the frozen driver records ToolOutcome.FailedAfterStart with no touched paths; no success value, partial result, handle or page token is produced. Handles and page tokens are registered only after the computation completed without cancellation. If the registry is disposed when they are registered, it registers nothing and the Effect throws java.util.concurrent.CancellationException with the same lifecycle and driver results. Expected read outcomes return normally. The read never waits for the EDT while it holds read access.

An unexpected platform failure during a read returns READ_FAILED with a category from a closed set and no source text, arguments or stack content. The first matching rule gives the category: PATH_RESOLUTION for a failure in the SR-004 path checks; INDEX_QUERY for a failure inside a name index, file name index or reference search call; DOCUMENT_READ for a failure while reading document text or line offsets; PSI_READ for every other failure at SR-026 steps 2 to 9. A violated domain invariant throws. Logs record only operation, category and counts. Every outcome that carries a hint (STALE_HANDLE, STALE_PAGE, INDEX_NOT_READY, TOO_MANY_RESULTS, SOURCE_TOO_LARGE, LINE_EXCEEDS_BYTE_CAP, UNSUPPORTED_LANGUAGE, READ_FAILED) names only catalog tools. The UNSUPPORTED_LANGUAGE hint names read_file and search_text as the labeled fallback.

Java domain values for read arguments, outcomes, handles, page tokens and the generic registry contain no IntelliJ platform, JSON or coroutine types. IntelliJ types, including smart pointers inside registry payloads, exist only in read adapters. The execution path uses no MCP, HTTP or runtime reflection, and no handle exposes a PSI pointer.

Every read outcome value is deeply immutable: it holds only strings, primitives, domain values and unmodifiable copies of collections, and no platform object. Changing an input collection after construction, or changing editor, index or file state, does not change an outcome that was already produced. Read outcomes appended as accepted tool results keep the CacheGeneration prefix invariant across changing IDE state.

Disposing the registry at New Session or content close invalidates every symbol handle, read handle and page token and releases every smart pointer. A later lookup returns STALE_HANDLE or STALE_PAGE. A handle from a disposed registry never resolves in a new registry. A read whose computation ends after disposal registers nothing and its Effect throws (SR-019).

Result ordering is deterministic: find_file by rendered path; search_symbols by qualified owner, name, signature, rendered path and start offset; get_file_outline in source order; find_references and search_text by rendered path, then start offset. Strings compare by UTF-16 code unit; an absent value sorts before any present value. Equal project state, equal registry state and equal arguments give equal outcomes, except that each get_symbol_info call issues a new read handle and each page result with more results issues a new page token.

Identity terms. A declaration range is the text range of the declaration PSI element in the current document, including its doc comment, annotations and modifiers, reported as 0-based start and end-exclusive UTF-16 offsets plus 1-based start and end lines. A signature is computed from source text without type resolution: for a method or constructor, the name followed by the parameter type texts in parentheses, separated by ', '; for a field or enum constant, the name; for a type, its qualified name. A parameter type text is the text of the parameter type element with comments and annotations removed, whitespace runs collapsed to one space, one '[]' appended for each array dimension written after the parameter name, and varargs written as '...'. A compact canonical constructor uses the record component types in declaration order. A signature does not prove identity; the handle does. The qualified owner of a member or nested type is the qualified name of the containing type; of a top-level type, its package name (empty for the default package). The containing declaration of a reference is the innermost enclosing catalog declaration, reported as qualified owner plus signature.

Failure precedence for one admitted read, first applicable wins: (1) cancellation, including a disposed registry at registration (SR-019); (2) PROJECT_UNAVAILABLE; (3) registry lookup of an input symbol handle, including an owner type handle (STALE_HANDLE), then of an input page token, including a different operation or argument set (STALE_PAGE), then the PSI modification count of the token (STALE_PAGE), all without waiting for indexing; (4) path outcomes in SR-004 order; (5) file-type and language outcomes (UNSUPPORTED_FILE, UNSUPPORTED_LANGUAGE), without waiting for indexing; (6) INDEX_NOT_READY for index-backed operations; (7) re-resolution STALE_HANDLE (SR-013), then NOT_A_TYPE (SR-006), then PSI modification count STALE_PAGE inside the operation computation (SR-017); (8) TOO_MANY_RESULTS; (9) the operation result, including RANGE_OUT_OF_BOUNDS, LINE_EXCEEDS_BYTE_CAP and SOURCE_TOO_LARGE. An unexpected platform failure at steps 2 to 9 returns READ_FAILED. Argument rejection (SR-001) happens before admission.

acceptance.when: Construct each read argument at, below and above every limit; with blank queries, queries containing CR or LF and queries of 1,001 UTF-16 units; with a search_symbols name that is not a Java identifier; with find_file queries containing '\', a leading or trailing '/', and empty, '.' and '..' segments; with read_file start and end omitted, end before start and a 301-line span; and with an unrestricted empty symbol name.
acceptance.then: Valid boundary values construct and omitted read_file lines default to 1 and start plus 99; every invalid value returns a named argument rejection; no operation reaches an adapter; the catalog contains exactly seven operations.

acceptance.when: In a fixture project with lines of exactly 10 KiB plus LF, read_file lines 1–5 of that file, a range across end of file, a start after end of file, an empty file, a file whose first line exceeds 24 KiB, a binary file, a text file above the content-loading limit, a directory, a missing project path, a missing path under an excluded directory, an existing excluded file, a missing and an existing absolute path outside the project, a symlink inside the project that points outside it, a non-Java text file by absolute path, a library source file by its jar URL and a class file in a library class root; separately, in a fixture whose project base directory is reached through a symbolic link, read_file a project file by its relative path and by its absolute path through the link.
acceptance.then: Lines 1–5 return exactly lines 1–2 with actual range 1–2 and truncated set; the end-of-file range is clipped to the last line; the empty file and the late start return RANGE_OUT_OF_BOUNDS with their line counts; LINE_EXCEEDS_BYTE_CAP is returned with the first line's exact byte size; the binary file and the file above the content-loading limit return UNSUPPORTED_FILE; the directory returns NOT_A_FILE; the missing project path returns FILE_NOT_FOUND; both excluded cases return EXCLUDED_PATH; both outside paths, the symlink and the class file return OUTSIDE_PROJECT; the text file and the library source succeed; the symlinked-base reads succeed and render the same '/'-separated path relative to the project base directory; successful reads return read handles with the observed version.

acceptance.when: Open a Java file in an editor and insert a new method with a unique name without saving, then call read_file, search_text, get_file_outline and search_symbols for it.
acceptance.then: All four report the new method from the unsaved text, with ranges that match the unsaved document and the unsaved document version.

acceptance.when: Run find_file for a name present in source, generated source, an excluded directory and a library source, with PROJECT and LIBRARIES scopes; also run find_file for 'a/B.java' where 'a/B.java' and 'xa/B.java' exist.
acceptance.then: PROJECT returns only the source file with origin PROJECT; LIBRARIES returns exactly the source file and the library file with their origins; the source file renders as its '/'-separated path relative to the project base directory and the library file as its jar URL; generated and excluded files are absent; paths are ordered; the suffix query returns only 'a/B.java'.

acceptance.when: Declare two overloads of one method name in one class, 'm(java.util.List<String> a)' and 'm(int... b)', and search_symbols for that name.
acceptance.then: Two distinct candidates with distinct handles are returned in SR-024 order with signatures 'm(java.util.List<String>)' and 'm(int...)'; neither is chosen silently.

acceptance.when: Declare two unrelated classes with the same simple name in different packages, reference only one of them, then search_symbols and find_references for each.
acceptance.then: Both classes are separate candidates with different qualified owners; find_references for the referenced class returns exactly its references, and for the other class returns a complete page with no references.

acceptance.when: Call get_file_outline on a Java file with nested classes, on a Java file with 101 catalog declarations, and on a non-Java text file, and call search_symbols restricted to the non-Java file.
acceptance.then: The Java outline lists only declarations in source order with handles, and each nesting depth equals the number of enclosing catalog declarations; the 101-declaration file returns a page of 100 entries with a next-page token and then a complete page of 1; the non-Java outline and the restricted search return UNSUPPORTED_LANGUAGE with a hint that names read_file and search_text and no other tool, never an empty success; no handle is issued for the non-Java file.

acceptance.when: Call get_symbol_info on the handle of a method that has a Javadoc comment and an annotation and is preceded in the file by a line containing a non-BMP character; then call it on a method longer than 300 lines.
acceptance.then: The first result has identity, a range that starts at the doc comment in UTF-16 offsets with 1-based lines, bounded source, current document version and a read handle whose range equals the returned range; the second returns SOURCE_TOO_LARGE with line count and byte size and no source and no read handle.

acceptance.when: A class Base declares m(); Derived extends Base, overrides m() and declares an overload m(int). Code contains a call derived.m(), a call base.m() through a Base-typed variable, a call derived.m(1), a plain comment and a string literal containing 'm', a Javadoc {@link Derived#m()}, an unrelated class with its own m(), and a call to that unrelated m(). Separately, a class Util declares a static method u(); another file has a static import of Util.u, a generated source calls Util.u(), and a non-Java fixture file holds a platform-resolved reference to Util. Call find_references for the handles of Derived.m, Base.m, Util.u and Util.
acceptance.then: Derived.m returns exactly the derived.m() call with kind CODE and containing declaration, and the Javadoc link with kind DOC; the base.m() call, the derived.m(1) call, the plain comment, the string literal and the unrelated method's call are absent. Base.m returns exactly the base.m() call; derived.m() is absent. Util.u returns the static import with kind IMPORT and no containing declaration, and the generated call with kind CODE and the generated flag set. Util includes the non-Java reference with kind CODE. Every page carries the target's kind, name, qualified owner, signature, declaration range and document version, and the scope PROJECT; each reference range starts at the referenced name.

acceptance.when: search_text a literal in a directory scope where matches differ by case, one match is in an unsaved editor, one file is generated, one is excluded, one is binary, one text file exceeds the content-loading limit, one line holds two non-overlapping matches, and one match starts at column 800 of a 2,000-unit line; also search_text with the binary file and with the file above the content-loading limit as the file scope.
acceptance.then: Only case-sensitive matches in current document text are returned; generated, excluded and binary files are absent; the skipped-file count is 1; the two matches on one line are two results; each result's start and end are document offsets; the long-line excerpt is the 500-unit window starting at column 700 with truncated set; both file scopes return UNSUPPORTED_FILE.

acceptance.when: Return the same element from search_symbols and get_file_outline, then submit a handle string that the registry never issued.
acceptance.then: Both operations return the same handle; the unissued handle returns STALE_HANDLE with a hint that names only catalog tools.

acceptance.when: Fill the registry past 2,048 entries with symbol handles, read handles and page tokens while refreshing one entry; look up a read handle identifier as a symbol handle and a symbol handle identifier as a page token; then dispose the registry, issue one more entry, and look up handles and page tokens from the disposed and a new registry, using a fake payload with a recording release action.
acceptance.then: The least-recently-used entry is evicted and returns STALE_HANDLE or STALE_PAGE by entry kind and its payload is released; the refreshed entry survives; the wrong-kind lookups return STALE_HANDLE and STALE_PAGE; after disposal the issue returns the disposed result and registers nothing, every handle returns STALE_HANDLE, every token STALE_PAGE and every payload is released once; nothing resolves in the new registry.

acceptance.when: Obtain a method handle, edit the document above the method and inside its body, call get_symbol_info; replace the whole method text with a method of another name at the same position and call get_symbol_info; obtain a second method handle, delete that method and call get_symbol_info again.
acceptance.then: After the edits above and inside the body the result reports the moved range, the current body and the new document version; after the replacement by another name and after deletion the result is STALE_HANDLE.

acceptance.when: With the index wait bound injected as 200 ms, enter dumb mode through the platform dumb-mode test utility and call search_symbols; call search_symbols again and leave dumb mode before the bound; call read_file and get_file_outline during dumb mode.
acceptance.then: The first call returns INDEX_NOT_READY with a catalog-only retry hint and no candidates after at least 200 ms; the second call returns results after indexing ends; read_file and get_file_outline succeed without waiting.

acceptance.when: Stop the run from the EDT while a read waits for indexing, and while a find_references computation blocks inside a test reference query executor on a latch that the test releases only after Stop; separately close the content while such a read blocks; separately dispose the registry, without cancelling the run, while a search_symbols computation blocks on such a latch; separately run a read whose CallAdmission returns Limited and one whose CallAdmission returns Rejected.
acceptance.then: Each cancelled or disposed call's admission status is FAILED_AFTER_START, the Effect threw java.util.concurrent.CancellationException, and the driver records ToolOutcome.FailedAfterStart with no touched paths; Stop returned before the latch was released; the Effect returned only after the blocked computation terminated; no handle or page token was registered; admission counted each read once; the read computation thread and the Effect calling thread were not the EDT; the Limited and Rejected reads return NotAdmitted with their admission result and made no IntelliJ call.

acceptance.when: Hold smart mode constant. Request page one of find_references with limit 1, make an unsaved document edit in the project, request page two; repeat without a change, then repeat the page-two request with the same token; request page one of search_text with limit 1, make an unsaved edit, request page two; reuse a token with a different limit, with another operation and in a new registry. Separately, with the index wait bound injected as 200 ms, request page one of search_symbols, enter dumb mode, and request page two.
acceptance.then: Unchanged state continues in deterministic order to a complete final page, and the repeated page-two request returns the same page again; both unsaved edits, the different limit, the other operation and the new registry return STALE_PAGE; the request after dumb-mode entry returns STALE_PAGE before 200 ms elapse.

acceptance.when: Make a read adapter throw an unexpected platform exception containing source text and a path, once during path checks, once inside reference search and once while reading document lines.
acceptance.then: The operation returns READ_FAILED with categories PATH_RESOLUTION, INDEX_QUERY and DOCUMENT_READ in that order; the outcome and captured log contain no source text, argument or stack content.

acceptance.when: Inspect compiled dependencies of the read domain package and read adapter package.
acceptance.then: Domain classes depend only on Java, annotations, lifecycle and run domain packages; IntelliJ types appear only in adapters; JSON, coroutine, MCP and HTTP types are absent.

acceptance.when: With a test ModelItemRenderer, produce read outcomes, append them as accepted tool results through CacheGeneration, then change editor text, reindex and delete a file, and append further read outcomes.
acceptance.then: Every consecutive request extends the previous bytes exactly; no prefix violation occurs. This is a regression test; AC-023 proves SR-022 immutability.

acceptance.when: With the index wait bound injected as 200 ms, let a test reference query executor start dumb mode while find_references executes; in one case leave dumb mode after the bound, in another before it.
acceptance.then: The first returns INDEX_NOT_READY with no partial references; the second returns the complete reference list after the computation restarts.

acceptance.when: In a Java file with a top-level class holding two explicit constructors, a nested class, a method m(String a[]), a field, a local class with a method, an anonymous class with a method and an initializer, plus an annotation type, an enum with constants one of which has a body with a method, and a record with a compact canonical constructor, call search_symbols with an empty name restricted to the file and restricted to the top-level class handle, and with the class name unrestricted. Also call search_symbols with an empty name restricted to a generated source file, restricted to a library class handle with scope PROJECT, and restricted to the handle of method m.
acceptance.then: The file restriction lists every catalog declaration at every depth, including the annotation type, the enum constants and the compact constructor with the record component types as signature; the class restriction lists only its two constructors, nested class, method and field; m has signature 'm(String[])'; local classes, anonymous classes, their methods, the enum-constant body method and initializers are absent; the unrestricted class-name query returns the class and its two constructors as separate candidates; the generated file restriction and the library class restriction list their declarations; the method handle restriction returns NOT_A_TYPE.

acceptance.when: With the result collection cap injected as 3, call find_references for a symbol with 4 references and search_text for a literal with 3 matches and limit 2.
acceptance.then: find_references returns TOO_MANY_RESULTS with a narrowing hint and no page; search_text returns a page of 2 with a next-page token and then a complete page of 1.

acceptance.when: Construct each read outcome from mutable input lists, then mutate the lists; in a fixture, produce outcomes, then edit, reindex and delete their files.
acceptance.then: Every outcome stays equal to a copy taken at construction; no outcome component type belongs to a platform package.

acceptance.when: In dumb mode, call get_symbol_info with an unissued handle, search_symbols restricted to a Kotlin file, and read_file with a missing path under an excluded directory; with a closed project, call get_symbol_info with an unissued handle; make path resolution throw an unexpected platform exception.
acceptance.then: The handle call returns STALE_HANDLE and the Kotlin call UNSUPPORTED_LANGUAGE, both without waiting for the index bound; read_file returns EXCLUDED_PATH; the closed-project call returns PROJECT_UNAVAILABLE; the injected failure returns READ_FAILED with category PATH_RESOLUTION.

acceptance.when: Attach a library with a sources jar and a second library without sources. Project code calls a method of the library-with-sources class. Call search_symbols for that class name and for the no-sources class name with PROJECT and LIBRARIES scope, then call find_references with PROJECT scope on the handle of the library class and of its called method.
acceptance.then: PROJECT returns no library candidate; LIBRARIES returns the class from the sources jar with its jar URL path and origin LIBRARY and returns no candidate for the class without sources; both find_references calls return the project reference that resolves to the compiled declaration.

type_safety_audit.invalid: An eighth read operation, a dispatcher operation, or an out-of-bound argument reaching an IntelliJ adapter
type_safety_audit.type_api_prevention: Sealed read-operation algebra with one record per operation; controlled factories return a validated argument or a named argument rejection
type_safety_audit.residual_runtime_obligation: Wire JSON is parsed into these factories by the later codec feature
type_safety_audit.justification: The seven-tool ceiling is a product contract; argument values come from an unsound boundary

type_safety_audit.invalid: A page, source block or excerpt larger than its bound
type_safety_audit.type_api_prevention: Bounded result collections and text values validate size at construction; limits and the collection cap are validated components; a sealed outcome has a TooManyResults variant without a page
type_safety_audit.residual_runtime_obligation: Adapter stops collecting at the collection cap plus one, sorts the collected results, then slices the page
type_safety_audit.justification: Output bounds are I12 correctness requirements, not tuning

type_safety_audit.invalid: Partial lines, a silently empty read, invented ranges, an over-span request, or binary bytes returned as text
type_safety_audit.type_api_prevention: Argument factory applies line defaults and rejects end before start and spans above 300; operation-local read_file outcome variants for success with actual range, range out of bounds, line cap exceeded and unsupported file
type_safety_audit.residual_runtime_obligation: Adapter computes line offsets on the document text observed in one read action
type_safety_audit.justification: Line structure and file type are runtime properties of the document

type_safety_audit.invalid: A read of an arbitrary filesystem path or of an excluded tree
type_safety_audit.type_api_prevention: Validated path argument plus a sealed path-resolution outcome whose variants follow the fixed check order; resolved file identity is constructible only by the adapter
type_safety_audit.residual_runtime_obligation: Adapter normalizes the path, resolves symbolic links and checks project file index membership under read access in the SR-004 order
type_safety_audit.justification: Filesystem layout and project roots are mutable external state

type_safety_audit.invalid: Excluded or generated files in PROJECT results, or library files without an explicit scope
type_safety_audit.type_api_prevention: Scope enum with PROJECT default; result entries carry rendered path (SR-004) and origin
type_safety_audit.residual_runtime_obligation: Adapter filters excluded and generated files with platform file index checks
type_safety_audit.justification: Generated-source classification is platform configuration

type_safety_audit.invalid: One candidate chosen for an ambiguous name, merged overloads, an unrestricted wildcard listing, a non-catalog declaration kind, a candidate without a qualified owner, or an owner restriction on a non-type
type_safety_audit.type_api_prevention: Candidate list type with one entry per resolved declaration; declaration kind enum limited to the catalog kinds; qualified owner is a required component; wildcard argument factory requires a restriction; sealed outcome with a NOT_A_TYPE variant
type_safety_audit.residual_runtime_obligation: Adapter enumerates every declaration the name index returns within scope and page, searches library sources with library sources included, omits declarations inside local classes, anonymous classes and enum-constant bodies, and checks the owner handle element kind
type_safety_audit.justification: Declaration sets depend on the live index

type_safety_audit.invalid: A raw AST dump, or an empty outline for an unsupported language
type_safety_audit.type_api_prevention: Outline entry type limited to declaration kinds; sealed outcome with UNSUPPORTED_LANGUAGE variant
type_safety_audit.residual_runtime_obligation: Adapter walks Java PSI declarations in a background read action without resolving types
type_safety_audit.justification: Language support is determined by the file type at runtime

type_safety_audit.invalid: Symbol information built from model-supplied text instead of a handle
type_safety_audit.type_api_prevention: Operation argument is a symbol handle value only; sealed outcome with a source variant that carries the read handle for exactly the returned range and a SourceTooLarge variant without source or handle
type_safety_audit.residual_runtime_obligation: Adapter re-resolves the handle before reading
type_safety_audit.justification: Identity must come from IntelliJ resolution (I5)

type_safety_audit.invalid: A text occurrence reported as a reference, a reference to an unrelated same-name symbol, or a call through a super method reported for an overriding method
type_safety_audit.type_api_prevention: Reference entry construction is adapter-only (package-private) with a closed kind enum and a generated flag; every page carries target identity and scope components
type_safety_audit.residual_runtime_obligation: Adapter uses platform reference search for the resolved element with strict method search, computes ranges from the element offset plus the reference range, and classifies kind from the enclosing import statement or doc comment
type_safety_audit.justification: Reference resolution is live platform behavior

type_safety_audit.invalid: Regex or case-insensitive matching, a whole-project scan without explicit scope, stale disk text, an excerpt that does not contain its match start, or a silent empty result for an unreadable file scope
type_safety_audit.type_api_prevention: Literal query value and required scope component; no regex or case option exists in the argument type
type_safety_audit.residual_runtime_obligation: Adapter scans current document text for literal non-overlapping matches, computes the excerpt window and counts skipped large files
type_safety_audit.justification: Text content and file classification are runtime state

type_safety_audit.invalid: A model-forged or content-derived handle, or two live handles for one element
type_safety_audit.type_api_prevention: Handle identifier constructible only by the registry; the registry offers issue-or-reuse with an adapter-supplied match predicate and never compares payloads itself
type_safety_audit.residual_runtime_obligation: Adapter compares a new smart pointer with live payload pointers using pointToTheSameElement before issuing
type_safety_audit.justification: Java cannot prevent a model from echoing arbitrary strings; resolution must reject them

type_safety_audit.invalid: Unbounded handle growth, an evicted handle resolving to a different element, an identifier resolving to a payload of another kind, or an entry registered after disposal
type_safety_audit.type_api_prevention: Final generic registry with a private bounded access-ordered map, one typed key per entry kind so that a lookup returns only that kind's payload, an opaque payload type parameter, a release callback, a sealed lookup outcome and a sealed issue outcome with a disposed variant
type_safety_audit.residual_runtime_obligation: Registry synchronizes issue, lookup, eviction and disposal; adapter supplies the release action
type_safety_audit.justification: Eviction order depends on runtime access sequence

type_safety_audit.invalid: A read that reports a deleted element, a replacement declaration as the handle's element, or pre-edit ranges for an edited document
type_safety_audit.type_api_prevention: Sealed resolution outcome with live and stale variants
type_safety_audit.residual_runtime_obligation: Adapter reads pointer and document version in one read action and compares the restored element's kind, name and signature with the handle payload
type_safety_audit.justification: Pointer survival after reparse is platform behavior

type_safety_audit.invalid: A read handle whose ranges or version change after issue
type_safety_audit.type_api_prevention: Final read-handle class with a controlled factory that validates range order, nonnegative offsets and line values of at least 1 and stores immutable ranges and version
type_safety_audit.residual_runtime_obligation: None in this feature; mutation features revalidate the version at commit
type_safety_audit.justification: Mutations in later features depend on this evidence

type_safety_audit.invalid: A result built from disk text while an editor holds unsaved changes, or PSI ranges from an uncommitted document
type_safety_audit.type_api_prevention: Result values carry the document version they were computed against
type_safety_audit.residual_runtime_obligation: Adapter runs every read computation under the documents-committed constraint
type_safety_audit.justification: Unsaved state exists only in the running IDE (I6)

type_safety_audit.invalid: An authoritative empty result during indexing, or an unbounded wait
type_safety_audit.type_api_prevention: Sealed readiness outcome shared by index-backed operations; the index wait bound is a validated injected positive duration
type_safety_audit.residual_runtime_obligation: Adapter runs index-backed platform calls only inside the smart-mode read computation with the bound and maps index-not-ready failures
type_safety_audit.justification: Indexing state changes at runtime and has no partial-result signal on the platform

type_safety_audit.invalid: A later page that silently skips or repeats items after a project change, or a replayed token that returns a different page
type_safety_audit.type_api_prevention: Continuation sum type Complete or More(token); token is a registry entry constructible only by the registry and bound to operation, arguments and count
type_safety_audit.residual_runtime_obligation: Adapter compares the current PSI modification count before the index wait and again inside the computation, and recomputes the page from the token offset
type_safety_audit.justification: Project PSI changes between model turns

type_safety_audit.invalid: A symbol handle issued for a non-Java PSI element
type_safety_audit.type_api_prevention: Adapter-only handle factory that accepts only Java declarations of catalog kinds; UNSUPPORTED_LANGUAGE variant in outline and restricted symbol search outcomes
type_safety_audit.residual_runtime_obligation: Adapter checks the file language before semantic access
type_safety_audit.justification: QUALIFICATION_TARGET limits qualification to Java

type_safety_audit.invalid: A read that bypasses admission, blocks the EDT, returns while its computation still runs, registers handles after Stop or disposal, reports partial results after Stop, or returns a completed result when admission refused
type_safety_audit.type_api_prevention: Read executor accepts only a CallAdmission and a RunCancellation and returns a sealed read execution result with operation-local outcome variants and a NotAdmitted variant carrying the admission result; handle registration happens after the computation result is obtained
type_safety_audit.residual_runtime_obligation: Adapter links the run cancellation token to the platform read computation with a nonblocking listener, awaits termination on the Effect thread, and throws java.util.concurrent.CancellationException on cancellation or a disposed registry
type_safety_audit.justification: Thread and cancellation behavior are runtime properties (I7, I8)

type_safety_audit.invalid: A swallowed platform exception reported as success, or source text in a log
type_safety_audit.type_api_prevention: READ_FAILED variant with a closed category enum and no free-form content; hint values are built only from catalog tool names; invariant checks throw
type_safety_audit.residual_runtime_obligation: Adapter catches platform exceptions at the boundary and maps them with the SR-020 category rule
type_safety_audit.justification: Platform failures are external; I10 forbids content in logs

type_safety_audit.invalid: PsiElement, VirtualFile, Document or JSON types in domain values
type_safety_audit.type_api_prevention: Separate domain and adapter packages; the registry is generic over an adapter payload type; package-private adapter construction
type_safety_audit.residual_runtime_obligation: Architecture test inspects compiled dependencies
type_safety_audit.justification: Build dependencies and later edits can break layering

type_safety_audit.invalid: An accepted read result whose content changes when the IDE state changes
type_safety_audit.type_api_prevention: Outcome values are final classes or records that copy collections into unmodifiable lists at construction and accept only domain component types
type_safety_audit.residual_runtime_obligation: Architecture test (AC-018) and value-equality test (AC-023); prefix regression (AC-019)
type_safety_audit.justification: I13 requires mutable IDE state never to change an existing prefix

type_safety_audit.invalid: An old-session handle resolving after New Session
type_safety_audit.type_api_prevention: Registry identity embedded in handle and token values; disposed registry rejects every lookup
type_safety_audit.residual_runtime_obligation: Session owner calls dispose at New Session and content close
type_safety_audit.justification: Session lifetime is owned by tool-window content (SESSION_OWNER)

type_safety_audit.invalid: Order that depends on index iteration or hash order
type_safety_audit.type_api_prevention: Ordered immutable result lists and one comparator per operation
type_safety_audit.residual_runtime_obligation: Adapter sorts collected results before paging
type_safety_audit.justification: Stable order is required for truthful paging and cache stability

type_safety_audit.invalid: A range that omits the doc comment, a line/column range in another unit, or a signature that depends on type resolution
type_safety_audit.type_api_prevention: Declaration range value with validated UTF-16 offsets and 1-based lines; signature value built by one adapter function from source text
type_safety_audit.residual_runtime_obligation: Adapter reads element text ranges from committed PSI and converts offsets to lines on the same document
type_safety_audit.justification: Later mutation features depend on the exact range; outlines must work without indexes

type_safety_audit.invalid: Two possible outcomes for one call, or a wait for indexing before a registry or path failure
type_safety_audit.type_api_prevention: One adapter pipeline with ordered stages, each returning a sealed stage outcome that short-circuits
type_safety_audit.residual_runtime_obligation: Adapter maps unexpected platform failures to READ_FAILED at each stage
type_safety_audit.justification: Deterministic outcomes are a workflow principle; the model must receive the same failure for the same state

non_goals: Wire JSON argument parsing, tool schemas, tool descriptions, the LLM status/code/content envelope and ToolOutcome content rendering
Mutations, handle invalidation on agent edits, formatting, diagnostics, build and test execution
Regex search, case-insensitive search, glob file patterns and whole-project unscoped text search
Semantic support or parity claims for languages other than Java
Session owner wiring, New Session UI and tool-window content lifetime integration beyond a registry dispose operation
Persisting handles, page tokens or read results across sessions
MCP, HTTP, idea-facade or any second index beside IntelliJ
Changing CAP-LIFECYCLE-ADMISSION or CAP-DOMAIN-RUN-DRIVER declarations or semantics
assumptions: CAP-LIFECYCLE-ADMISSION is frozen with FINAL_GATE_PASS; its S3 is blocked only on EV-SURFACE. This feature relies on its admission semantics, and this feature's S3 cannot close while lifecycle S3 remains blocked.
CAP-DOMAIN-RUN-DRIVER is closed; reads bind to its PlannedCall.ToolOperation, ToolRunner and CallAdmission surfaces without changing them.

A read cancelled after admission, or finding a disposed registry at registration, throws java.util.concurrent.CancellationException from the Effect; the frozen driver maps it to ToolOutcome.FailedAfterStart with the message 'Tool execution failed after admission: CancellationException' and no touched paths (NativeRunDriver.executeOne). The frozen driver acts on the ToolRunner's returned NotStarted reason for refused admission (NativeRunDriver.kt:156-179), so the codec maps the NotAdmitted read result as SR-019 states. The codec feature renders expected read outcomes into ToolOutcome content and cannot change lifecycle accounting.

IntelliJ JUnit 5 test fixtures for a Java project with editors, libraries, generated and excluded roots, dumb mode and a test reference query executor are available through the IntelliJ Platform Gradle test framework configuration; the design may change plugin-core/build.gradle.kts for this and must keep tests discoverable as @Test methods.

Name and file indexes throw IndexNotReadyException in dumb mode (FileBasedIndexImpl). Reference search executors that are not dumb-aware block until smart mode when called without read access (QueryExecutorBase.java:57-66), so SR-016 requires calls inside the read computation. Dumb-mode entry runs a write action (DumbServiceImpl.kt:335-342), and a write action cancels a running non-blocking read computation, which reruns only when its constraints hold again (NonBlockingReadActionImpl.java:639-641,808-814). The platform exposes no partial-result signal for reference search; completeness is only complete or more results.

Only the document modification stamp changes on unsaved edits; the view provider stamp stays at the last committed stamp. The PSI modification count changes on committed physical PSI changes and on dumb-mode entry and exit, not on uncommitted edits.

Smart pointers return no element after the element is deleted. After the element's text is replaced, restore by element info can bind to a replacement declaration at the same range (SmartPsiElementPointerImpl.java:90-115), so SR-013 compares the restored kind, name and signature with the handle payload.
The Structure View builder is not relied on for outlines because background use is not established; outlines walk Java PSI declarations in a background read action.

Normalizations of product bounds: limit 1–100 with default 50 for find_references; 300 lines and 24 KiB for get_symbol_info source with SOURCE_TOO_LARGE above it; 1,000 UTF-16 units for text queries; LINE_EXCEEDS_BYTE_CAP as the explicit error for a start line above 24 KiB (product 'smaller read or explicit unsupported error').

Normalizations of product terms: SR-025 range, signature, owner and containing-declaration definitions; SR-006 catalog declaration kinds; SR-003 line model and defaults; SR-004 path rendering and check order; SR-010 match and excerpt rule and skipped-file count; SR-020 READ_FAILED category rule; SR-026 failure precedence; SR-001 query validation; SR-004 canonical root comparison; SR-009 reference range, line and kind; SR-010 document offsets and match column; SR-025 parameter type text, array dimensions and compact constructors; SR-012 entry kinds.

Normalizations of scope: generated sources are omitted from find_file, unrestricted search_symbols and search_text directory scans, and included and marked in find_references so reference sets stay complete; handle reuse for the same element (SR-011) keeps one live handle per element in the registry.
The product rule 'reports partial search/index readiness separately' is satisfied by fail-closed INDEX_NOT_READY and TOO_MANY_RESULTS outcomes, because the platform gives no partial-result signal.

Java short-name stub lookups hide library source files unless library sources are included (JavaSourceFilterScope.java:36-51). A project reference to a compiled library class or method is equivalent to the declaration in its attached source (PsiClassImplUtil.java:1162-1228,1251-1273), so find_references on a library source handle finds project references.

The PSI modification count also changes for document and VFS changes to project-content files whose PSI is not loaded (PsiDocumentManagerBase.java:1149,1314; PsiVFSListener.java:139-148), so SR-017 staleness covers find_file and search_text over unloaded files.
